subject: angol
title: A gap year before further studies
instructionsHu: Vitatkozz a vizsgáztatóval az alábbi állításról. A kiosztott álláspontod: az állítás MELLETT érvelsz – ezt az álláspontot a vita során nem változtathatod meg. Fejtsd ki az érveidet, reagálj a vizsgáztató ellenérveire, és próbáld meggyőzni őt.

debate.statement: Every school leaver should take a gap year before going to university or starting work
candidateIdeas: After twelve years of school, students need a break to avoid burnout.
A gap year helps young people find out what they really want to study or do.
Travelling, volunteering or working builds independence and life skills.
Work experience makes CVs and university applications stronger.
Students who have taken a gap year often start university more motivated.
examinerArguments: Many students lose their study habits and never go back to education.
A gap year can be expensive, so it is only an option for wealthy families.
It delays starting a career and earning money by a whole year.
Some employers may see a gap year as a waste of time.
Students can travel and work during the summer holidays instead.
Not everyone needs a break; some people know exactly what they want.

followUpQuestions: Isn't there a danger that students lose their motivation and never continue their studies?
A year of travelling costs a lot. What about students from poorer families?
Why can't students do all this during the summer holidays?

usefulPhrases.hu: kihagy egy évet a tanulmányai előtt

usefulPhrases.en: It doesn't have to cost a fortune.
usefulPhrases.hu: Nem kell, hogy egy vagyonba kerüljön.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Let's discuss this statement: 'Every school leaver should take a gap year before going to university or starting work.' What do you think?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I think it's an excellent idea. After twelve years of school and the stress of the school-leaving exams, most students are close to burnout. A gap year gives them time to rest and, more importantly, to find out what they really want to study. Several of my older friends dropped out after their first semester because they had chosen the wrong course.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Isn't there a danger that students lose their motivation and never continue their studies?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: There's a risk, I admit, if the year is spent doing nothing. That's why it should be a structured year – working, volunteering or travelling with a plan. From what I've read, students who have taken a gap year often start university more motivated, not less.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: A year of travelling costs a lot. What about students from poorer families?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: That's a fair point, but a gap year doesn't have to mean backpacking around Asia. You could work for a local company for six months and earn money, which also makes your CV much stronger.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Why can't students do all this during the summer holidays?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Because two months simply isn't enough to gain real work experience or to become independent – you've barely settled in before it's time to go back. That said, I accept that some people know exactly what they want. But even for them, a year in the real world would be valuable, so universities should make it easier, for example by letting students defer their place.

notes: Feladat teljesítése: a vizsgázó végig a kiosztott álláspontot (az érettségi utáni szabadév mellett) képviseli, érveit tapasztalattal támasztja alá (idősebb barátok, akik rossz szakot választottak), az ellenérvekre részben egyetértve reagál, a végén pedig úgy keres kompromisszumot, hogy közben nem adja fel az álláspontját.

Szókincs: a téma pontos szavai (burnout, drop out, a structured year, defer their place, CV) és változatos vitafordulatok (There's a risk, I admit; That's a fair point, but …; That said, I accept that …).
Nyelvhelyesség: B2-es szerkezetek hibátlanul – Past Perfect (had chosen), Present Perfect (who have taken), szenvedő szerkezet (is spent), 'doesn't have to mean' és 'by letting students …'.
Érdemes megtanulni: „close to burnout”, „doesn't have to mean”, „you've barely settled in”, „That said, I accept that …”.
